limitations_and_boundaries: The study primarily uses chemogenetic models in mice; human relevance remains to be established.
The role of immunoglobulins in normal circuit dynamics or development is not addressed.
The specific antigens recognized by IgM in the CNS are unknown.
The contribution of other immunoglobulin isotypes cannot be ruled out, though sIgM KO data suggest they are insufficient.
The J20 AD model may not fully recapitulate human AD immune interactions.
The 5-day chemogenetic paradigm may not capture longer-term synaptic changes.
The KA model did not produce measurable synapse loss, limiting conclusions from that paradigm.
Potential confounding effects of surgical damage or viral transduction were controlled but not completely eliminated.
The study does not examine whether similar innate-adaptive interactions occur in other brain circuits.
